notes.title: manifold M
notes.content: The manifold M (Skolem constant for the universally quantified object).

notes.title: 3-manifold
notes.content: M is a 3-dimensional manifold.

notes.title: closed
notes.content: M is closed: compact and without boundary.

notes.title: simply connected
notes.content: The fundamental group of M is trivial.

notes.title: hypotheses
notes.content: M is a simply connected, closed 3-manifold.

notes.title: 3-sphere
notes.content: The 3-dimensional sphere S³.

notes.title: homeomorphic to S³
notes.content: M is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere S³.

notes.title: Poincaré Conjecture
notes.content: Every simply connected, closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere S³.

notes.title: standard piece P
notes.content: A generic standard piece of the decomposition (free variable, implicitly universal).

notes.title: S² × S¹
notes.content: The product of the 2-sphere and the circle.

notes.title: ℝP³ # ℝP³
notes.content: Connected sum of two real projective 3-spaces; π₁ = ℤ/2 * ℤ/2.

notes.title: finite connected sum
notes.content: M is homeomorphic to a finite connected sum of standard pieces.

notes.title: P is a standard piece
notes.content: P occurs as a factor in the connected-sum decomposition of M.

notes.title: spherical space form
notes.content: P is homeomorphic to S³/Γ for a finite group Γ acting freely by isometries.

notes.title: classification of pieces
notes.content: Every standard piece is a spherical space form, S² × S¹ (or its unorientable variant), or ℝP³ # ℝP³.

notes.title: pieces are simply connected
notes.content: Every factor of the decomposition of M is simply connected.

notes.title: every piece is S³
notes.content: Every standard piece of the decomposition of M is homeomorphic to S³.

notes.title: cite: van Kampen
notes.content: Fundamental group of a connected sum is the free product of the factors' groups; a free product is trivial iff every factor is trivial.

notes.title: cite: π₁ of the pieces
notes.content: Among the standard pieces, only S³ (Γ = 1) is simply connected.

notes.title: cite: S³ idempotent
notes.content: A finite connected sum of copies of S³ is homeomorphic to S³.

53c5be962bd7.statement: \mathrm{sorry}(\text{proof of } ⟦02b022ba06c5⟧ \text{ via Ricci flow with surgery: existence for all time, finite-time extinction from } \pi_3 \neq 0 \text{, finitely many surgeries, and reversal of the surgery history})

notes.title: HOLE: Ricci flow machinery
notes.content: Everything analytic lives here: Perelman existence of the flow with surgery, Colding–Minicozzi finite-time extinction, volume bound on surgery count, and the topological reconstruction of M by undoing surgeries.

07063e73256e.statement: \mathrm{sorry}(\text{proof of } ⟦02abbe5cdbc6⟧ \text{ via the canonical neighborhood classification of manifolds covered by } \varepsilon\text{-necks and caps})

notes.title: HOLE: canonical neighborhood classification
notes.content: Classification of closed 3-manifolds entirely covered by canonical neighborhoods (ε-necks and ε-caps).

notes.title: step: pieces simply connected
notes.content: π₁(M) is the free product of the factors' fundamental groups; since π₁(M) = 1, every factor's group is trivial.

notes.title: step: pieces are S³
notes.content: Each piece is one of the classified types and is simply connected; the group computation eliminates all but S³.

notes.title: step: M ≅ S³
notes.content: M is a finite connected sum of copies of S³, hence homeomorphic to S³.

notes.content: Discharge the hypotheses to conclude the Poincaré conjecture.
